`lua`: Lua interpreter.

## Synopsis

<strong>lua</strong> \[<em>options</em>\] \[<em>script</em> \[<em>args</em>...\]\]

## Description

<strong>lua</strong> is Lua's standalone interpreter, as <em>lua.c</em> is. It runs Lua given as text: statements from <strong>-e</strong>, a <em>script</em> file, standard input, or lines typed at its interactive prompt (the REPL).

Every mcos program is already Lua: the kernel starts each process through the loader, <em>/lib/ld.lua</em>, which opens the standard library and runs the program, so programs do not need <strong>lua</strong> to run. <strong>lua</strong> is a program like any other.

Options are handled in order: <strong>-e</strong> and <strong>-l</strong> run as they are met, then the <em>script</em> runs with <em>args</em> as its <strong>...</strong> and in the global table <strong>arg</strong>: <strong>arg\[0\]</strong> is the script, <strong>arg\[1\]</strong> on its arguments, and the interpreter and its options at negative indices. What the script returns is ignored.

With no script and no <strong>-e</strong> or <strong>-v</strong>, <strong>lua</strong> starts the REPL if standard input is a terminal, and otherwise runs standard input as a script.

An error is reported on standard error as <strong>lua:</strong> <em>message</em> followed by a stack traceback (the interpreter's own frames left out).

## Options

<strong>-e</strong> <em>stat</em>
: Run the statement <em>stat</em>.

<strong>-l</strong> <em>mod</em>
: Require module <em>mod</em> into the global <em>mod</em>.

<strong>-l</strong> <em>g</em><strong>=</strong><em>mod</em>
: Require module <em>mod</em> into the global <em>g</em>.

<strong>-i</strong>
: Enter the REPL after running <em>script</em> (and print the version first).

<strong>-v</strong>
: Print the version.

<strong>-E -W</strong>
: Accepted, and do nothing.

<strong>--</strong>
: Stop handling options.

<strong>-</strong>
: Stop handling options and run standard input.

The argument of <strong>-e</strong> and <strong>-l</strong> may also be joined to it (<strong>-lfs</strong>).

## The repl

The prompt is <strong>\></strong> ; a line that is an incomplete statement goes on at <strong>\>\></strong> . A line is first tried as an expression; its values are printed, separated by tabs, a table as its contents (readably, through <em>/lib/serialization.lua</em>), other values as <strong>print</strong> shows them.

Lines are read with <em>/lib/readline.lua</em> and its keys:

<strong>Left Right Home End ^A ^E</strong>
: Move the cursor.

<strong>Ctrl+Left Ctrl+Right</strong>
: Move a word back or on, as bash does (Alt+Left and Alt+Right too).

<strong>Backspace Delete ^D</strong>
: Erase the character before or under the cursor.

<strong>^U ^K ^W</strong>
: Cut the line before the cursor, after it, or the word before it.

<strong>Up Down</strong>
: Go through the history (100 lines).

<strong>^L</strong>
: Clear the screen.

<strong>Tab</strong>
: Complete a Lua name: a global, or a field of the table named before the last <strong>.</strong> or <strong>:</strong> (methods through <strong>\_\_index</strong> too). A table's name gets a <strong>.</strong>, a function's a <strong>(</strong>. A second Tab lists the choices.

<strong>^C</strong>
: Drop the line being typed; while code runs, end it with <strong>interrupted!</strong> at its next system call (code that makes none runs on).

<strong>^D</strong>
: On an empty line, leave the REPL.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 on a bad option, or if a chunk given by <strong>-e</strong>, <strong>-l</strong>, the script or standard input fails to load or raises an error.

## Examples

```text
lua -e "print(2^10)"
lua -l fs -e 'print(fs.isdir("/tmp"))'
lua script.lua one two
echo "print(1+1)" | lua
```

## Notes

<strong>-E</strong> and <strong>-W</strong> have no effect: there are no <strong>LUA\_INIT</strong> variables and warnings go nowhere.

## See also

<strong>sh</strong>(1), <strong>edit</strong>(1)
